course.title: 认识 AI，从这里开始
course.description: 从一张真实照片和一个小问题开始，学会交代任务、辨认依据、检查结果，并决定什么事情仍由你作主。
course.audience: 完全初学的成年人；不需要编程经验。可先用本课提供的真实公开材料完成判断与小作品。
objectives: 用真实材料区分回答、查找与执行。
说明自己的任务，核对来源、范围与重要条件。
在新情境中选择工具、帮助程度与需要自己确认的步骤。

en.title: Understanding AI: From Fear to Confidence
en.description: Start with real examples, try small decisions, and learn when AI can help, what to check and which choices stay yours. No programming required.
en.audience: Adult beginners. No programming experience is required. Start with the real public material provided in the course.
objectives: Distinguish an answer, a lookup and an action using real source material.
Describe a task and check its sources, scope and important conditions.
Choose tools, useful help and human checks when the situation changes.

lessons.title: 怎样让 AI 把照片讲给没看到的人听？
lessons.content:
# 怎样让 AI 把照片讲给没看到的人听？

假设你在看太空摄影展，想把眼前的照片讲给没来的家人听，却只说得出“一个球、一片灰”。

先说照片要讲给谁听，再追问具体细节；需要来历时，把记录一起给 AI。

::play{#ask-about-a-picture-v2}

[Be My Eyes：图片功能介绍](https://www.bemyeyes.com/blog/introducing-be-my-ai/) · [NASA：《地出》照片记录](https://www.nasa.gov/image-article/apollo-8-astronaut-bill-anders-captures-earthrise/)

en.title: How to get AI to describe a photo to someone who hasn't seen it
en.content:
# How to get AI to describe a photo to someone who hasn't seen it

Imagine you're at a space photography exhibition and want to describe a photo to family members who couldn't come, but all you can manage is "a ball and a patch of gray."

First, tell AI who you're describing it for, then ask follow-up questions for specific details. When you need its background, share the record along with it.

::play{#ask-about-a-picture-v2}

[Be My Eyes: Introducing Be My AI](https://www.bemyeyes.com/blog/introducing-be-my-ai/) · [NASA: Apollo 8 Astronaut Bill Anders Captures Earthrise](https://www.nasa.gov/image-article/apollo-8-astronaut-bill-anders-captures-earthrise/)

exercises.title: 给家人写一段带来历的介绍
exercises.prompt:
家人还想知道这张照片的来历。NASA 的照片记录已经备好，这次由你决定怎样向 AI 提要求。
写两句话：一句描述画面，一句根据记录说明拍摄背景。

en.title: Write a photo introduction with background context for family
en.prompt:
Your family also wants to know the story behind this photo. The NASA record is ready for you—this time, it's up to you how to prompt AI.
Write two sentences: one describing what's in the image, and one explaining the background based on the record.
rubric: The prompt clearly requests a visual description and the background based on the attached record, rather than just poetic reflections.
The final two sentences describe the visible relationships among the Earth, the lunar surface, or the black background, using natural phrasing without requiring a fixed word order.
The background matches the NASA record: Bill Anders, December 24, 1968, Apollo 8 lunar orbit; not described as a moon landing, nor confusing the 2022 webpage date with the photo date.

No fabricated thoughts or feelings of the photographer. If the initial AI output does not meet the criteria, the learner is allowed to revise the prompt or refine the final piece before re-evaluating.
请求明确需要画面描述和依据所附记录的拍摄背景，而不是只要求诗意感想。
最终两句话描述地球、月面或黑色背景中的可见关系，允许合理的自然语言，不要求固定词序。
背景与 NASA 记录一致：Bill Anders，1968 年 12 月 24 日，阿波罗 8 号绕月；不写成登月，也不把 2022 年网页日期当拍摄日期。
没有编造摄影者心理活动。AI 初次结果不符合时，允许学习者修改请求或最终作品后再评估。

activities.title: 怎样让 AI 把照片讲给没看到的人听？
activities.brief: 你需要一段让人听得明白的描述，可以请 AI 帮忙，再追问关心的细节。
activities.goal: 写两句话：一句描述画面，一句根据记录说明拍摄背景。
activities.takeaway: 先说照片要讲给谁听，再追问具体细节；需要来历时，把记录一起给 AI。
activities.hint: 先看手头的材料，按实际需要来用。

source.label: NASA：《地出》照片记录

strings.怎样让 AI 把照片讲给没看到的人听？: How can you get AI to describe a photo to someone who hasn't seen it?
strings.你需要一段让人听得明白的描述，可以请 AI 帮忙，再追问关心的细节。: You need a description that's easy to follow. You can ask AI for help, then follow up on the details you care about.
strings.写两句话：一句描述画面，一句根据记录说明拍摄背景。: Write two sentences: one describing the image, and one explaining the background based on the record.
strings.先说照片要讲给谁听，再追问具体细节；需要来历时，把记录一起给 AI。: Start by telling AI who the description is for, then follow up on specific details; when you need its backstory, share the record with AI too.
strings.先看手头的材料，按实际需要来用。: Review the materials at hand and use them based on what you need right now.
strings.Be My Eyes 曾用看图与追问帮助盲人和低视力用户。我们用 NASA 的《: Be My Eyes has used image descriptions and follow-up questions to help blind and low-vision users. We'll practice this approach using NASA's Earthrise photo.
strings.Be My Eyes：图片功能介绍: Be My Eyes: Image Feature Overview
strings.Be My Eyes 给盲人和低视力用户提供图片描述和追问功能，也保留了联系真人: Be My Eyes provides image descriptions and follow-up questions for blind and low-vision users, while still keeping an option to connect with human volunteers.
strings.功能介绍不代表每次图片描述都准确。重要细节你仍要核对。: A feature overview doesn't mean every image description will be accurate. You still need to verify key details.
strings.网页发表于 2022 年 12 月 23 日；照片拍摄于 1968 年。: The webpage was published on December 23, 2022; the photo was taken in 1968.
strings.NASA 记录：Bill Anders 于 1968 年 12 月 24 日，在: NASA record: Bill Anders took Earthrise on December 24, 1968, during Apollo 8's lunar orbit.
strings.这份记录能证实拍摄者和拍摄日期，没写他按快门时在想什么。: This record confirms the photographer and the date, but it doesn't say what he was thinking when he pressed the shutter.
strings.NASA 保存的《地出》。先观察照片里的景物、颜色和位置。: NASA's Earthrise photo. Start by observing the scene, colors, and positions in the picture.
strings.Bill Anders 于 1968 年 12 月 24 日，在阿波罗 8 号绕: Bill Anders took Earthrise on December 24, 1968, while orbiting the Moon on Apollo 8. This was not a moon landing. The corresponding webpage was published on December 23, 2022; the webpage date is not the date the photo was taken.
strings.请用两句话描述这张照片。: Please describe this photo in two sentences.
strings.这条请求可能得到什么？: What might you get from this request?
strings.画面里有哪些东西，是什么样子。: What is in the image and what it looks like.
strings.主要介绍拍摄者和照片背后的故事。: Mainly introduces the photographer and the story behind the photo.
strings.主要写看到照片的感想。: Mainly thoughts and reflections on seeing the photo.
strings.看看 AI 实际说了什么: See what the AI actually said
strings.用刚才那条请求运行一次，对照你的预想。: Run that prompt once and compare it with what you predicted.
strings.挑一处，让描述更具体: Pick one detail to make the description more specific
strings.家人没有看到照片。你最想让他看清哪一处？对照 AI 的回答，找出值得补充的细节。: Your family member hasn't seen the photo. Which part do you most want them to picture clearly? Compare with the AI's response to find details worth adding.
strings.好的追问不是只说“再详细一点”，而是指出你关心什么，例如地球的颜色，或地球与月面: A good follow-up isn't just saying 'be more detailed.' It specifies what you care about, such as the Earth's colors or where it sits relative to the lunar surface. If the AI has already explained something clearly, there's no need to ask again.
strings.能只凭照片知道是谁拍的吗？: Can you tell who took the photo just from the image itself?
strings.拍摄者和拍摄日期来自 NASA 的照片记录，不是画面里写着这些字。要让 AI 介: The photographer and date come from NASA's photo record—they aren't written on the image. If you want the AI to explain the background, provide that record to the AI as well.
strings.Be My Eyes 这个例子说明了什么？: What does the Be My Eyes example show?
strings.它在 2023 年推出了图片描述与继续追问，也保留真人志愿者帮助。这个例子展示了: In 2023, it introduced image descriptions and follow-up questions while keeping help from human volunteers. This example shows real-world use, not a guarantee that every description will be accurate.
strings.在照片上挑一个部分，写一句你想追问的细节。: Pick a part of the photo and write one detail you want to ask more about.
strings.注意蓝白色的部分。你还想知道它的颜色、形状，还是位置？: Notice the blue and white area. Do you want to ask about its color, shape, or position?
strings.月面在画面下方。你想让家人怎样想象它与地球的位置？: The Moon's surface is at the bottom of the frame. How do you want your family to picture where it is relative to Earth?
strings.黑色背景与地球、月面形成对比。选你真正想讲清的一点。: The black background contrasts with Earth and the Moon. Pick the one detail you really want to explain clearly.
strings.把想追问的细节加进去: Add the details you want to ask about
strings.现在让原来的请求更贴近家人的需要。加上刚才想问的细节，再对比新旧描述。: Now tailor your original request to your family's needs. Add the detail you wanted to ask about, then compare the new description with the old one.
strings.让没看到照片的人，更容易想象你关心的部分。: Make it easier for someone who hasn't seen the photo to picture what you care about.
strings.说明这是讲给没看照片的人听，并指出一个细节。不要只加“更详细”三个字。: Mention that this is for someone who hasn't seen the photo, and specify a detail. Don't just add the words 'be more detailed.'
strings.给家人写一段带来历的介绍: Write an introduction with background for your family
strings.家人还想知道这张照片的来历。NASA的照片记录已备好，这次由你决定怎么向 AI: Your family also wants to know the story behind this photo. The NASA photo record is ready—now it's up to you to decide how to ask AI.
strings.你希望 AI 写给谁看？这两句话分别讲什么？: Who do you want AI to write this for? What should each of the two sentences say?
strings.画面描述能和照片对上。: The description matches what is shown in the photo.
strings.拍摄者、拍摄日期和任务来自给出的记录。: The photographer, date, and mission come from the provided record.
strings.没有把想象的故事或心情写成事实。: Imagined stories or feelings are not presented as facts.
strings.下次遇到自己的照片，也可以先说用途，再围绕具体细节追问。照片的来历要用对应资料确: Next time with your own photos, you can also state the purpose first, then follow up on specific details. Always verify a photo's background with reliable sources.
strings.假设你在看太空摄影展，想把照片讲给没来的家人听，让他们也能想象眼前的画面。: Imagine visiting a space photography exhibition and wanting to describe a photo to family who aren't there so they can picture the scene.

investigate.title: 挑一处，让描述更具体
investigate.brief: 家人没有看到照片。你最想让他看清哪一处？对照 AI 的回答，找出值得补充的细节。
investigate.explanation: 好的追问不是只说“再详细一点”，而是指出你关心什么，例如地球的颜色，或地球与月面的位置。AI 已经讲清的部分，不必再问一遍。

more.question: 能只凭照片知道是谁拍的吗？
more.answer: 拍摄者和拍摄日期来自 NASA 的照片记录，不是画面里写着这些字。要让 AI 介绍来历，把对应记录也提供给 AI。

more.question: Be My Eyes 这个例子说明了什么？
more.answer: 它在 2023 年推出了图片描述与继续追问，也保留真人志愿者帮助。这个例子展示了真实用途，并不保证每次描述都准确。

game.instruction: 在照片上挑一个部分，写一句你想追问的细节。

regions.label: 地球
regions.note: 注意蓝白色的部分。你还想知道它的颜色、形状，还是位置？

regions.label: 月面
regions.note: 月面在画面下方。你想让家人怎样想象它与地球的位置？

regions.label: 黑色背景
regions.note: 黑色背景与地球、月面形成对比。选你真正想讲清的一点。

modify.title: 把想追问的细节加进去
modify.brief: 现在让原来的请求更贴近家人的需要。加上刚才想问的细节，再对比新旧描述。
modify.goal: 让没看到照片的人，更容易想象你关心的部分。
modify.suggestion: 说明这是讲给没看照片的人听，并指出一个细节。不要只加“更详细”三个字。

make.title: 给家人写一段带来历的介绍
make.scenario: 家人还想知道这张照片的来历。NASA的照片记录已备好，这次由你决定怎么向 AI 提要求。
make.goal: 写两句话：一句描述画面，一句根据记录说明拍摄背景。
make.promptPlaceholder: 你希望 AI 写给谁看？这两句话分别讲什么？
checklist: 画面描述能和照片对上。
拍摄者、拍摄日期和任务来自给出的记录。
没有把想象的故事或心情写成事实。

finish.title: 把这段照片介绍带走
finish.note: 下次遇到自己的照片，也可以先说用途，再围绕具体细节追问。照片的来历要用对应资料确认。

lessons.title: 没听清一段录音，怎样让 AI 帮你整理？
lessons.content:
# 没听清一段录音，怎样让 AI 帮你整理？

朋友分享了一小段英文录音，你没听清，想先留成文字，再讲给中文家人听。

先留下原话，再按需要翻译或概括；三种结果不要混用。

::play{#sound-words-and-meaning-v2}

[Whisper 发布介绍](https://openai.com/index/whisper/) · [Whisper 仓库测试录音](https://github.com/openai/whisper/blob/86098128c0b4f24f0e2aa2994de830614b474227/tests/jfk.flac)

en.title: Didn't catch an audio clip clearly? How AI can help sort it out
en.content:
# Didn't catch an audio clip clearly? How AI can help sort it out

A friend shared a short English audio clip that you didn't catch clearly. You'd like to save it as text first, then explain it to your Chinese-speaking family.

Save the original words first, then translate or summarize as needed; don't mix these three results together.

::play{#sound-words-and-meaning-v2}

[Whisper Announcement](https://openai.com/index/whisper/) · [Whisper Repository Test Audio](https://github.com/openai/whisper/blob/86098128c0b4f24f0e2aa2994de830614b474227/tests/jfk.flac)

en.front: What is the difference between audio transcription, translation, and summarization?
en.back: Transcription records the spoken words in the original language, translation switches to another language, and summarization extracts the main idea. Decide on the intended use before making a request.

cards.back: 转写留下原语言的讲话文字，翻译换一种语言，概括提炼主要意思。先看用途再提要求。

exercises.title: 给家人发一句简短说明
exercises.prompt:
家人这次不想逐句读英文，只想知道录音大致说了什么。自己向 AI 提要求，整理成能直接发出的中文消息。
用一句或两句中文说清主要意思，让人知道这是大意，不是逐字原话。

en.title: Send a brief note to family
en.prompt:
This time, your family doesn't want to read English line by line—they just want to know roughly what the audio said. Prompt the AI yourself and turn the result into a Chinese message ready to send.
Explain the main idea in one or two Chinese sentences, making it clear that this is a summary rather than verbatim quotes.
rubric: The prompt asks for a summary for Chinese-speaking family members, rather than only requesting the verbatim English.

The final Chinese text is concise and preserves the main contrast of 'ask not what your country can do for you, ask what you can do for your country'; natural paraphrasing is permitted without requiring fixed wording.
Does not introduce policy details, character emotions, or action specifics not found in the audio, and does not require learners to agree with the viewpoint.
States that it is a summary or paraphrase without disguising it as verbatim English quotes; various appropriate expressions are acceptable.
请求针对给中文家人看的大意，而不是只要求英文原话。
最终中文简短，保留“不要只问国家能为自己做什么，也要思考自己能为国家做什么”的主要对比，可自然转述，不要求固定措辞。
不添加录音中没有的政策、人物情绪或行动细节，不要求学习者赞同观点。
说明是大意或转述，不伪装为逐字英文原话；不同合适表达都可通过。

source.label: Introducing Whisper

strings.没听清一段录音，怎样让 AI 帮你整理？: Didn't catch an audio clip? How AI can sort it out for you
strings.先留下原话，再按需要翻译或概括，能避免把几种不同任务混在一起。: Keep the original words first, then translate or summarize as needed, so different tasks don't get mixed together.
strings.用一句或两句中文说清主要意思，让人知道这是大意，不是逐字原话。: Explain the main point in a sentence or two of Chinese, making it clear that this is a summary, not a verbatim quote.
strings.先留下原话，再按读者需要翻译或概括；三种结果不要混用。: Keep the original words first, then translate or summarize based on what the reader needs; keep the three outputs distinct.
strings.先看手头的材料，按当前用途处理。: Review the material at hand first, then handle it according to the task.
strings.朋友分享了一小段英文录音，你没听清，想先留成文字，再讲给中文家人听。: A friend shared a short English audio clip that you didn't quite catch. You want to turn it into text first, then explain it to your Chinese-speaking family.
strings.Whisper 是 OpenAI 介绍过的语音识别系统。我们用它开源仓库里的一段: Whisper is a speech recognition system introduced by OpenAI. We'll test it with an actual sample from its open-source repository.
strings.这是 OpenAI 的发布介绍。练习里的用途和请求属于教学设定，不是发布介绍里的: This is OpenAI's release announcement. The scenarios and prompts in this exercise are pedagogical examples, not recordings or execution logs from the announcement.
strings.OpenAI 于2022年9月21日介绍 Whisper 语音识别系统。发布内容: On September 21, 2022, OpenAI introduced the Whisper speech recognition system. The release covered transcribing audio in its original language and translating other languages into English.
strings.单个测试录音不能代表所有语音的识别效果。本课先实际转写，再由文字 AI 翻译或概: A single test recording cannot represent recognition quality across all speech. In this lesson, we transcribe the audio first, then have a text AI translate or summarize it.
strings.固定版本的原始测试录音；本课仅转换文件格式。: Original test recording from a fixed release; this lesson only converts the file format.
strings.开源测试实际读取 jfk.flac 并执行转写。: The open-source test actually reads jfk.flac and runs transcription.
strings.单一录音不能代表所有录音识别效果。: A single recording cannot represent recognition performance for all audio.
strings.Whisper 仓库的英文测试录音: English Test Audio from the Whisper Repository
strings.这段录音长 11 秒，来自 Whisper 仓库的 jfk.flac 测试文件。: This 11-second audio clip comes from the jfk.flac test file in the Whisper repository. It is a converted version of the original recording, not synthesized speech.
strings.请按原语言转写这段录音，不翻译，不总结。: Please transcribe this recording in its original language, without translating or summarizing.
strings.按这条请求运行，先会拿到哪种文字？: If you run this request, what kind of text will you get first?
strings.录音里的英文原话。: The original English spoken in the recording.
strings.省去细节后的简短概括。: A brief summary without the details.
strings.把录音实际转成文字: Actually transcribe the audio into text
strings.转写是把听到的话按原语言记成文字。生成后，可以回听录音核对。: Transcription means turning speech into text in the original language. Once it's generated, you can listen back to verify.
strings.原话记录、译文和概括各有用途。下面用同一段话的几个例子，分清它们改变了什么。: Verbatim transcripts, translations, and summaries each have their uses. Below are examples from the same clip to see what each one changes.
strings.转写保留讲话的语言；翻译换一种语言表达意思；概括只保留主要意思。后两种不能当作逐: Transcription preserves the spoken language; translation expresses the meaning in another language; summarization keeps only the main points. Neither of the latter two should be treated as verbatim quotes.
strings.Whisper 能把任意语言互相翻译吗？: Can Whisper translate between any two languages?
strings.2022 年的发布介绍包括按原语言转写，以及把其他语言语音译成英文。这里的中文翻: The 2022 release announcement covered transcribing in the original language and translating foreign speech into English. The Chinese translation and summary here are done by a text AI, so this shouldn't be counted as Whisper translating between arbitrary languages.
strings.转写稿可以直接引用吗？: Can the transcript be quoted directly?
strings.重要句子要回听核对。录音噪声、停顿或发音可能造成错漏，听不清的地方先标出来，别靠: Be sure to listen back and verify important sentences. Background noise, pauses, or pronunciation quirks may cause errors, so mark unclear spots first instead of guessing what was said.
strings.Ask not what your country can do for you: Ask not what your country can do for you; ask what you can do for your country.
strings.这仍是录音里的英文原话。这里只摘出了一句，实际引用仍需回听。: This is still the original English from the recording. Only one sentence is excerpted here, so you still need to listen back before quoting it.
strings.不要问国家能为你做什么，要问你能为国家做什么。:
不要问国家能为你做什么，要问你能为国家做什么。
English meaning: “Ask not what your country can do for you; ask what you can do for your country.”
strings.这里把意思换成中文，不再是英文原话。: This translates the meaning into Chinese and is no longer the original English quote.
strings.这段话鼓励人们主动贡献，而不是只等待帮助。: This statement encourages people to contribute proactively rather than just waiting for help.
strings.这是示例里的大意概括，省去了原句的具体说法，不是逐字引语。: This is an example summary of the main idea; it leaves out the original wording and is not a verbatim quote.
strings.保留原话，再加一层中文意思: Keep the original words and add an explanation in Chinese
strings.你已经有了英文记录。家人看中文更方便，可以让 AI 在保留原话的同时，补上中文解: You already have the English transcript. Since reading Chinese is easier for your family, you can have AI keep the original words while adding a Chinese explanation.
strings.让原话和中文解释各自清楚，不要把两者混在一起。: Keep the original quote and the Chinese explanation distinct so they don't get mixed together.
strings.说明要保留英文原话，中文用来解释意思，并给两部分加上不同标题。: Specify that the original English should be kept, use Chinese to explain the meaning, and give both sections distinct headings.
strings.给家人发一句简短说明: Send a brief note to your family
strings.家人这次不想逐句看英文，只想知道录音大致说了什么。你自己提要求，整理成能直接发出: This time your family doesn't want to read the English word by word—they just want the gist. Specify what you need and turn it into a Chinese message ready to send.
strings.这次给谁看？需要原话、译文，还是大意？: Who is this for? Do you need the original words, a translation, or the gist?
strings.保留原句的主要意思，不额外添加观点。: Keep the main point of the original sentence without adding extra claims.
strings.文字简短，中文家人能看懂。: Keep the message brief so your Chinese-speaking family can easily understand it.
strings.能看出是大意或转述，不冒充逐字原话。: Make sure it clearly reads as a summary or paraphrase, not a word-for-word quote.
strings.把适合家人看的文字带走: Take the text that works best for your family
strings.收到别的录音时，先想好要原话、译文还是概括。重要内容还是要回听核对。: When you receive other recordings, first decide whether you need the original words, a translation, or a summary. Always listen back or verify important details.

more.answer: 重要句子要回听核对。录音噪声、停顿或发音可能造成错漏，听不清的地方先标出来，别靠猜补成原话。

cards.text: Ask not what your country can do for you; ask what you can do for your country.
cards.why: 这仍是录音里的英文原话。这里只摘出了一句，实际引用仍需回听。

cards.text: 不要问国家能为你做什么，要问你能为国家做什么。
cards.why: 这里把意思换成中文，不再是英文原话。

cards.text: 这段话鼓励人们主动贡献，而不是只等待帮助。
cards.why: 这是示例里的大意概括，省去了原句的具体说法，不是逐字引语。

modify.title: 保留原话，再加一层中文意思
modify.brief: 你已经有了英文记录。家人看中文更方便，可以让 AI 在保留原话的同时，补上中文解释。
modify.goal: 让原话和中文解释各自清楚，不要把两者混在一起。
modify.suggestion: 说明要保留英文原话，中文用来解释意思，并给两部分加上不同标题。

make.title: 给家人发一句简短说明
make.scenario: 家人这次不想逐句看英文，只想知道录音大致说了什么。你自己提要求，整理成能直接发出的中文消息。
make.goal: 用一句或两句中文说清主要意思，让人知道这是大意，不是逐字原话。
make.promptPlaceholder: 这次给谁看？需要原话、译文，还是大意？
checklist: 保留原句的主要意思，不额外添加观点。
文字简短，中文家人能看懂。
能看出是大意或转述，不冒充逐字原话。

finish.title: 把适合家人看的文字带走
finish.note: 收到别的录音时，先想好要原话、译文还是概括。重要内容还是要回听核对。

lessons.title: 想让 AI 写出你要的内容，怎样提要求？
lessons.content:
# 想让 AI 写出你要的内容，怎样提要求？

假设你想给家长群分享一个往年观月活动的例子。公告里的信息不少，直接转发一大段，别人不容易找到重点。

说清给谁看、拿来做什么、写成什么样；还没想好时，先要少量样例。

::play{#name-the-result-v2}

[OpenAI：怎么写清请求](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10032626-prompt-engineering-best-practices-for-chatgpt) · [NASA：2023 年观月夜公告](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/celebrate-international-observe-the-moon-night-at-nasas-goddard-space-flight-center/)

en.title: How to Ask AI to Write What You Need
en.content:
# How to Ask AI to Write What You Need

Suppose you want to share an example of a past moon-watching event with a parents' group. The announcement has plenty of information, and forwarding a long block of text makes it hard for others to spot the key details.

Make it clear who it's for, what it's used for, and how it should look; if you haven't decided yet, ask for a few short examples first.

::play{#name-the-result-v2}

[OpenAI: How to write clear prompts](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10032626-prompt-engineering-best-practices-for-chatgpt) · [NASA: 2023 Observe the Moon Night announcement](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/celebrate-international-observe-the-moon-night-at-nasas-goddard-space-flight-center/)

exercises.title: 换给筹备活动的同事看
exercises.prompt:
同事想借鉴活动点子，不需要照抄日期地点。这次把公告中选出的四项活动，整理成一项一行的灵感清单。
让同事看清四种活动分别是什么，不增加公告没有的物资数量或做法。

en.title: Adapting It for Colleagues Planning the Event
en.prompt:
Your colleagues want to borrow event ideas without copying the dates and locations. This time, organize four activities chosen from the announcement into a line-by-line list of ideas.
Make sure they can clearly see what each of the four activities is, without adding material quantities or instructions not found in the announcement.
rubric: The prompt clearly asks for an itemized list of activity ideas, rather than an event invitation or a long science article.

The final output includes four source activities: eclipse art creation, space rock exhibits, demonstrating moon phases with cookies, and lunar lander design; accurate synonymous translations are accepted.
One item per line or a clear list, without requiring dates or locations unnecessary for this task.
No material quantities, budgets, or guaranteed outcomes beyond the source material are added, and it is not written as an invitation to an active event.
请求清楚指向活动点子的分项清单，不要求一篇活动邀请或长科普。
最终作品包含四项来源活动：日食艺术创作、太空岩石展示、用饼干演示月相、月球着陆器设计；接受准确的近义译法。
一项一行或清楚的项目列表，不强制本任务不需要的时间地点。
没有添加资料之外的物资数量、预算或保证效果，不写成当前仍可参加的活动邀请。

intro.connection: 我们用 NASA 在 2023 年发布的观月夜公告练习，把“介绍一下”改成具体用途。

sources.note: 这是 OpenAI 帮助中心的写作指南。资料访问日期是 2026-09-15；本课任务和预览属于教学设计。
sources.summary: OpenAI 的指南建议把请求写清楚、写具体，带上相关背景；需要时说明语气，并检查、修改生成的结果。
sources.limitation: 这是写作建议，不是证明生产力必然提高的实验；没有特殊说法能保证答案正确。本课按用途挑短消息或清单，就是把这些建议用在教学里。

sources.note: NASA 在 2023 年 10 月 16 日发布的活动公告。资料记录的访问日期是 2026-09-15；本课的改写和选项属于教学设计。
sources.summary: NASA 这则公告讲的是 2023 年 10 月 21 日的观月夜。地点在马里兰州格林贝尔特的戈达德访客中心，时间是美国东部夏令时间（EDT）晚 6 点至 9 点，无需报名，风雨无阻。活动包括日食艺术创作、太空岩石展示、用饼干演示月相和月球着陆器设计。
sources.limitation: 这是历史公告，不是现在的活动邀请。课里的改写不是 NASA 官方批准的通知。没指定目标时区时，保留 EDT，别自己换算。公告提到活动项目，不等于安排了志愿者分工。

options.label: 可能是一段完整介绍。
可能列成几项信息。

run.title: 看看这次得到了哪种写法
run.note: 先按这条简单请求运行。暂时不用评“好不好”，看看它合不合家长群的需要。

investigate.title: 把重点排到容易找到的位置
investigate.brief: 同一份信息可以有不同排法。试着把家长先关心的内容放前面，再比较段落与分行资料卡。
investigate.explanation: 只给主题，AI 就得猜用途。想好给谁看、用来做什么，就能把想要的形式和必须保留的信息说出来。

more.question: 还没想好要哪种形式呢？
more.answer: 可以先让 AI 给几个短例子，比较之后再决定。不必在第一次请求里把所有条件定死。

game.instruction: 移动信息块，试两种排法。材料没有换，改变的是读起来的顺序。

modify.title: 把家长群的用途写进请求
modify.brief: 刚才试了排法。现在把你想要的样子告诉 AI，看看新结果是否更方便阅读。
modify.goal: 写成给家长看的简短资料卡，保留活动时间、地点和主要内容，注明是往年活动。
modify.suggestion: 可以说明读者、分项格式和不能遗漏的信息。保留 EDT，别让读者误以为是自己所在时区的时间。

make.title: 换给筹备活动的同事看
make.scenario: 同事想借鉴活动点子，不需要照抄日期地点。这次把公告中选出的四项活动，整理成一项一行的灵感清单。
make.goal: 让同事看清四种活动分别是什么，不增加公告没有的物资数量或做法。
make.promptPlaceholder: 同事需要什么清单？哪些信息这次可以不写？
checklist: 一项一行，方便逐项查看。
不编造预算、物资数量或额外活动。

finish.title: 一份适合当前用途的清单
finish.note: 同一份资料，给家长看和给筹备者看，重点可以不同。先说明用途，再判断结果是否合用。

lessons.title: 只想改一句，怎样让 AI 别把整篇都动了？
lessons.content:
# 只想改一句，怎样让 AI 别把整篇都动了？

你已经写好一段活动介绍，日期地点也核对过了。只有“活动很多，内容丰富”太笼统，却不想让 AI 把整篇重新写一遍。

指出改哪里、改成什么、保留什么；目标变了，允许的修改范围也可以变。

::play{#edit-one-part-v2}

[Canvas 发布介绍](https://openai.com/index/introducing-canvas/) · [NASA：2023 年观月夜公告](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/celebrate-international-observe-the-moon-night-at-nasas-goddard-space-flight-center/)

en.title: Just Want to Change One Sentence: How to Keep AI from Rewriting Everything?
en.content:
# Just Want to Change One Sentence: How to Keep AI from Rewriting Everything?

You've already written an event description and verified the date and location. Only "There are many activities with rich content" is too vague, but you don't want AI to rewrite the entire piece from scratch.

Point out where to change, what to change it to, and what to keep; when the goal changes, the permitted scope of edits can change as well.

::play{#edit-one-part-v2}

[Introducing Canvas](https://openai.com/index/introducing-canvas/) · [NASA: 2023 International Observe the Moon Night Announcement](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/celebrate-international-observe-the-moon-night-at-nasas-goddard-space-flight-center/)

exercises.title: 这次允许重排整篇
exercises.prompt:
现在要把介绍做成手机上好查的资料卡。原来三个段落不必逐字保留，但事实不能丢。
由你给 AI 提新要求，把全文整理成时间、地点、活动和参与安排四项。

en.title: Allow Reorganizing the Whole Piece This Time
en.prompt:
Now turn the introduction into a reference card that's easy to check on a phone. The original three paragraphs don't need to be kept word for word, but the facts cannot be lost.
Give AI a new request to organize the full text into four sections: time, location, activities, and participation details.
rubric: The request explicitly allows reorganizing the full text, instead of still requiring the original sentences to remain word for word.
The work is clearly divided into time, location, activities, and participation details.
Retain October 21, 2023, 6 to 9 p.m. EDT, NASA Goddard Visitor Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, no registration required, and rain or shine, allowing natural translations.
Retain the four selected activities, keep the historical tone so it does not mislead readers as a current invitation, and add no facts absent from the source.
请求明确允许重排全文，而不是仍要求原句逐字不动。
作品按时间、地点、活动和参与安排清楚分项。
保留 2023 年 10 月 21 日、晚 6 至 9 点 EDT、马里兰州格林贝尔特戈达德游客中心、无需报名和风雨无阻，允许自然译法。
保留四项选定活动，历史语气不误导为当前邀请，不添加来源没有的事实。

activities.title: 只想改一句，怎样让 AI 别把整篇都动了？
activities.brief: 这次练习把修改的位置和范围说清楚。
activities.goal: 由你提出新要求，把全文整理成时间、地点、活动和参与安排四项。
activities.takeaway: 指出改哪里、改成什么、保留什么；目标变了，允许的修改范围也可以变。

source.label: Introducing canvas

strings.只想改一句，怎样让 AI 别把整篇都动了？: How do you get AI to change just one sentence without rewriting the whole thing?
strings.这次练习把修改的位置和范围说清楚。: This exercise focuses on clearly stating where and how much to edit.
strings.由你提出新要求，把全文整理成时间、地点、活动和参与安排四项。: Set new requirements yourself to organize the text into four sections: time, location, activities, and participation details.
strings.指出改哪里、改成什么、保留什么；目标变了，允许的修改范围也可以变。: Specify what to change, what to change it to, and what to keep. When goals shift, the allowed scope of edits can change too.
strings.先看手头的材料，按当前用途处理。: Look at the materials on hand first, then adapt them to your current purpose.
strings.你写好了一段活动介绍，日期地点也核对过。只有“活动很多，内容丰富”太笼统，又不想: You've drafted an event description and checked the date and location. The phrase 'lots of diverse activities' is too vague, but you don't want AI to rewrite the entire piece.
strings.Canvas 的发布介绍演示过选中某段单独修改。我们接着用这份 NASA 公告和: The Canvas release demo showed how to select and edit a single section. We'll practice using this NASA announcement and draft.
strings.OpenAI 的 Canvas 发布介绍；本课用的是里面的写作协作场景。: OpenAI's Canvas release announcement; this lesson focuses on its collaborative writing scenario.
strings.这份介绍里讲了：在草稿旁并排改写、选中某段单独提意见、直接动手改，还有恢复早期版: This introduction covers: side-by-side editing, selecting sections for targeted feedback, editing directly, and restoring earlier versions.
strings.这些是 2024 年发布时的功能，不保证现在每个账户界面都一样，也不能证明某条修: These features reflect the 2024 release. Account interfaces may vary today, and no edit prompt is guaranteed to work every time. This lesson does not teach specific button layouts.
strings.NASA：2023 年观月夜公告: NASA: 2023 Observe the Moon Night Announcement
strings.NASA 的2023年观月夜历史公告；这是本课草稿活动事实的出处。: NASA's 2023 Observe the Moon Night archive announcement; this is the factual source for our draft.
strings.公告邀请公众于2023年10月21日美国东部夏令时间（EDT）晚6点至9点，到马: The announcement invites the public to the Goddard Visitor Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, on October 21, 2023, from 6 to 9 p.m. EDT. The event is rain or shine and requires no registration. Activities include eclipse art, space rock displays, cookie moon phase demonstrations, and lunar lander design challenges.
strings.这是已经过去的活动。本课草稿是教学改写，不是 NASA 官方通知。没有指定目标时: This is a past event. The draft here is an educational adaptation, not an official NASA notice. Do not convert EDT without a specified target time zone.
strings.① 这场观月夜安排在 2023 年 10 月 21 日晚 6 点至 9 点 ED:
① This Moon Night event was scheduled for October 21, 2023, from 6:00 PM to 9:00 PM EDT at the Goddard Visitor Center in Greenbelt, Maryland.
② There are many activities with rich content.
③ No registration was required at the time, rain or shine.
strings.原公告中的四项活动: Four activities from the original announcement
strings.日食艺术创作、太空岩石展示、用饼干演示月相、月球着陆器设计。这是从原公告选出的四: Eclipse art, space rock displays, moon phases with cookies, and lunar lander design. These are four activities selected from the original announcement, not the full lineup.
strings.请把草稿的第二句写具体一些。: Please make the second sentence of the draft more specific.
strings.这条请求没有说其他句子怎么办，你觉得会怎样？: This prompt doesn't say what to do with the other sentences. What do you think will happen?
strings.可能只修改第二句。: It might only modify the second sentence.
strings.可能连其他句子的说法也一起改。: It might also rewrite the other sentences.
strings.要看改稿，不能先认定修改范围。: You have to check the revision—you can't just assume what will change.
strings.看看这次实际改了哪里: See what actually changed this time
strings.拿原稿对照新稿。改得符合要求就可以保留，不必故意找错。: Compare the new draft against the original. If it meets your requirements, you can keep it—no need to look for flaws on purpose.
strings.亲手改一处，其余保持原样: Edit one spot by hand and keep the rest as is
strings.这是练习草稿，不是刚才的 AI 回复。先亲手补全那句笼统的话，你会更清楚该给 A: This is a practice draft, not the AI response from earlier. Flesh out that vague sentence yourself first, and you'll have a clearer idea of what to ask of AI.
strings.“改得更好”没有指出范围。说清改哪句、补什么，以及其他哪些句子不动，结果才方便对: Saying "make it better" doesn't define a scope. Clearly state which sentence to edit, what to add, and which other sentences to keep unchanged, so it's easy to verify the result.
strings.不是。只补一句时可以限定范围；要是改做资料卡，就可以允许重排全文。修改范围由你的: No. You can limit the scope when just adding one sentence, but if you're making a reference card, you can allow a full rewrite. The scope should be determined by your goal.
strings.选中“活动很多”那句，把原公告中的四项活动写具体。: Select the sentence "There are many activities" and flesh out the four activities from the original announcement.
strings.例如先写“活动包括……”，再补上四项内容。: For example, start with "Activities include..." and then fill in the four items.
strings.① 这场观月夜安排在 2023 年 10 月 21 日晚 6 点至 9 点 ED: ① This International Observe the Moon Night is scheduled for the evening of October 21, 2023, from 6 to 9 PM EDT at the Goddard Visitor Center in Greenbelt, Maryland.
strings.② 活动很多，内容丰富。: ② There are plenty of activities and lots to do.
strings.③ 当时无需报名，风雨无阻。: ③ At the time, no registration was required, and it was rain or shine.
strings.把修改范围明确告诉 AI: Clearly tell AI the scope of changes
strings.回到原请求，把需要保留的部分也说清楚。重新运行后，比较第二句和其余两句是否都符合: Return to your original prompt and clearly specify what to keep. After running it again, check whether the second sentence and the other two sentences meet your requirements.
strings.第二句说清四项活动；第一句和第三句保持原样。: Specify the four activities in the second sentence, while keeping the first and third sentences unchanged.
strings.指出具体句子和要补的内容，再说明哪些句子不动。实际改稿仍可能没照做，所以还要对照: Point out the specific sentence and what to add, then clarify which sentences should stay untouched. The revised draft might still not follow instructions completely, so you still need to check.
strings.这次允许重排整篇: Allowing a full reorganization this time
strings.现在要把介绍存成手机上容易查的资料卡。原来的三个段落不必逐字保留，但其中的事实不: Now you want to turn the description into a quick-reference mobile info card. The original three paragraphs don't need to be kept word-for-word, but none of the facts can be lost.
strings.这次允许改到什么范围？哪些内容必须保留？: What scope of changes is allowed this time? What content must be kept?
strings.明确允许按新用途重排全文。: Explicitly allow reorganizing the entire text for its new purpose.
strings.日期、含 EDT 的时间、地点和参与安排准确。: The date, time (including EDT), location, and attendance details are accurate.
strings.四项活动保留，并说明是往年记录。: Keep all four activities and note that they are past records.
strings.让修改范围跟着用途走: Let the edit scope follow the purpose
strings.局部修改就指出局部，重排全文就明确授权。看改稿时，按你原先的要求检查，而不只是看: Point out specific parts for partial edits, and give explicit permission when reorganizing the full text. When reviewing revisions, check against your original requirements rather than just whether it reads smoothly.

lessons.title: 缺了具体信息，怎样让 AI 帮你查？
lessons.content:
# 缺了具体信息，怎样让 AI 帮你查？

你想把往年的观月活动写进分享，却只记得大致名字，不确定是哪一天、在哪里。直接让 AI 写完整介绍，可能把缺的信息一起猜进去。

说清具体对象和缺什么；找到资料后，确认它说的是同一件事，再用来写作。

::play{#answer-or-search-contrast-goal-r2}

[ChatGPT Search 发布介绍](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-search/) · [NASA：2022 年观月夜公告](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/celebrate-international-observe-the-moon-night-with-nasa/) · [NASA：2023 年观月夜公告](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/celebrate-international-observe-the-moon-night-at-nasas-goddard-space-flight-center/)

en.title: Missing specific details? How to have AI look them up for you
en.content:
# Missing Specific Details? How to Have AI Look Them Up for You

You want to include a past Moon Night event in a post, but you only remember its general name—not the date or location. If you ask AI to write a full overview directly, it might guess and fill in the missing details.

Clearly state the specific event and what's missing; once you find the materials, confirm they refer to the exact same event before using them in your writing.

::play{#answer-or-search-contrast-goal-r2}

[Introducing ChatGPT Search](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-search/) · [NASA: 2022 Observe the Moon Night Announcement](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/celebrate-international-observe-the-moon-night-with-nasa/) · [NASA: 2023 Observe the Moon Night Announcement](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/celebrate-international-observe-the-moon-night-at-nasas-goddard-space-flight-center/)

exercises.title: 换一份记录，自己查清楚
exercises.prompt:
朋友想了解另一年的观月参与方式。这次查 2022 年公告，把活动日和参与形式写成两句可分享的说明。
日期和参与方式来自同一份 2022 年记录，附来源，并说明是往年信息。

en.title: Switch to another record and find the facts yourself
en.prompt:
A friend wants to know how to participate in Moon Night in another year. Look through the 2022 announcement this time, and write two shareable sentences covering the event date and ways to take part.
The date and participation details must come from the same 2022 record, include the source, and note that this is past information.
rubric: The prompt targets the event date and participation details from the 2022 announcement, rather than the 2023 Goddard event.
The final note states that the event date is October 1, 2022, and the in-person, online, or hybrid participation format comes from the same announcement.
Does not mistake the September 23, 2022 publication date for the event date, and does not mix in the location, time, or registration details from the 2023 Goddard event.
Keeps the corresponding NASA source or a clear source citation, and notes that this is past information; two natural sentences are sufficient, with no fixed wording required.
请求针对 2022 年公告的活动日及参与形式，而不是 2023 年戈达德场。
最终说明活动日为 2022 年 10 月 1 日，现场、线上或混合参与形式来自同一份公告。
不把 2022 年 9 月 23 日发表日当活动日，不混入 2023 年戈达德场的地点、时间或报名安排。
保留对应 NASA 来源或明确来源标识，并说明是往年信息；两句自然表达即可，不要求固定措辞。

lessons.title: 交给别人之前，这段请求还缺什么？
lessons.content:
# 交给别人之前，这段请求还缺什么？

## 给没到现场的朋友做一份回看说明

[美国国会图书馆的2024年国家图书节记录](https://www.loc.gov/events/2024-national-book-festival)记载了当时公布的安排：活动定于2024年8月24日举行，部分节目将直播，全部节目的录像会后提供。你的朋友没能到现场，希望知道怎样了解这些节目。

你先写了一句请求：“请介绍这个图书节，写得自然，不要太长。”现在准备把它连同原页面交给助手。

## 先猜一下

与朋友真正要做的事情相比，这句请求还缺哪一项关键信息？

先写下你的判断，再往下看答案。

## 答案

它没有说明要给没到现场的人做回看导览。先把读者、成品和需要检查的范围说清楚，才知道哪种介绍真的有用。

## 自己写出一份可以照着做的请求

用三句话就可以开始：材料是哪一页；给谁做什么；成品必须保留哪些条件。你来写第一版，不必照抄一个万能格式。

写好后，对照原页面检查：“部分节目将直播”和“全部录像会后提供”有没有被混成一件事？历史年份有没有被改成现在？

:::detail[把这些要求都写进去，会不会变得太复杂？]
你不需要同时规定字号、语气、段落长度和几十条规则。先保留最影响这份成品的几项：朋友没到现场，目的是了解节目，材料是2024年的记录。然后把两种观看方式分开，免得一句话把“部分直播”改成“全部直播”。这几项都有用，因为它们决定朋友看完说明后会怎么理解。其他表达可以留给助手选择。你写完后也能直接检查，不必只说喜欢或不喜欢。[明确目标与相关背景的指导](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10032626-prompt-engineering-best-practices-for-chatgpt)可以支持这种写法，但这段请求和最终编辑稿都是我们自己的工作，不是图书馆的原文。
:::

把这份请求里的各部分放到正确的位置。它们分别告诉助手使用什么、交出什么、以及怎样算完成。

::play{#first-request-checkpoint-sort}

### 改一处，再保住已经对的部分

若第一版太长，就只要求缩短文字，并明确保留年份与观看范围。修改以后，用同一页面重新核对那两项。最后留下一份请求和一段你自己检查过的短说明。

:::detail[还没有实际运行助手，我现在能完成哪一部分？]
先写好请求与检查条件，再自己做一份简短编辑稿，也能发现要求是不是清楚。比如你写“介绍图书节”，却发现无论怎么缩短都不知道该删什么，往往是读者用途还没定；你写明给不能到场的人看，就知道优先说明回看方式。之后使用可用的助手时，再把真实结果放到同一条件下检查。没有运行工具的编辑稿，不叫模型实测；已经运行的结果，也不能因为读起来漂亮就跳过核对。你要带走的是一套可以由你判断对错的工作方式，而不是一次无法解释的好运气。
:::

:::detail[完成说明以后，应该把什么一起留下？]
保留你使用的原页面入口和最后一次检查的要点。这样，朋友追问哪句话从哪里来时，你能找到对应信息；你以后把说明改给另一种读者时，也知道哪些历史事实不能随手替换。无需保存所有试过的措辞，也不用把每次犹豫写成长报告。留下能帮助下一次继续工作的东西：成品、来源、仍需确认的事项。
:::

## 自检

现在把这份短说明改给只想挑选一个节目观看的人。请重新写一条请求，保留原材料，修改读者用途，并写出一个需要重新检查的条件。

## 一句话

**把材料、成品和检查条件连起来，你就能从“请帮我写”走到“我知道它是否写对”。**

en.title: Before Handing It to Someone Else, What Is This Request Still Missing?
en.content:
# Before Handing It to Someone Else, What Is This Request Still Missing?

## Write a Catch-Up Guide for a Friend Who Couldn't Attend

[The Library of Congress record of the 2024 National Book Festival](https://www.loc.gov/events/2024-national-book-festival) notes that the event was scheduled for August 24, 2024, that some sessions would be livestreamed, and that recordings of all sessions would be available after the event. Your friend was unable to attend in person and wants to know how to follow these programs.

You first write a request: “Please introduce this book festival. Write naturally and keep it fairly short.” Now you are ready to hand it over to the assistant along with the original page.

## Predict first
Compared to what your friend actually needs to do, which key piece of information is this request still missing?

Write down your judgment first before reading on to the answer.

## Answer
It doesn't explain that you are making a catch-up guide for someone who couldn't attend in person. Only by first clarifying the reader, the deliverable, and the scope to check can you know what kind of introduction is genuinely useful.

## Write an Actionable Request Yourself

You can start with just three sentences: which page the source material comes from; who you are making what for; and what conditions the deliverable must preserve. Write the first draft yourself—there's no need to copy a one-size-fits-all format.

Once written, check it against the original page: Were “some sessions would be livestreamed” and “all recordings would be available after the event” conflated into a single thing? Was the historical year changed to the present?

:::detail[Will including all these requirements make it too complicated?]
You don't need to specify font size, tone, paragraph length, and dozens of rules all at once. First, keep the few items that most affect this deliverable: your friend couldn't attend in person, the goal is to learn about the programs, and the source material is the 2024 record. Then separate the two viewing options so a single sentence doesn't turn “some livestreamed” into “all livestreamed.” These items are useful because they determine how your friend will understand the explanation after reading it. Other phrasing choices can be left to the assistant. Once you finish writing, you can also verify it directly, rather than just saying whether you like or dislike it. [Guidance on clarifying goals and relevant context](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10032626-prompt-engineering-best-practices-for-chatgpt) supports this approach, but this prompt and the final edited draft are our own work, not the library's original text.
:::

Put each part of this request into its correct position. They tell the assistant what to use, what to deliver, and what counts as finished.

::play{#first-request-checkpoint-sort}

### Change One Thing, Then Protect What Is Already Right

If the first draft is too long, simply ask to shorten the text while explicitly preserving the year and viewing scope. After making revisions, check those two items against the same source page again. Finally, keep one request and one short guide that you have verified yourself.

:::detail[Without actually running the assistant yet, which part can I complete right now?]
Drafting the request and check criteria first, and then creating a brief edited draft yourself, will also reveal whether your requirements are clear. For example, if you write “introduce the book festival” and find that no matter how you try to shorten it, you don't know what to cut, it's often because the reader's purpose hasn't been defined yet; when you clearly state that it is for someone who cannot attend, you know to prioritize explaining how to watch the recordings. Later, when you use an available assistant, you can check the real output under those same conditions. An edited draft created without running the tool does not count as an actual model test; nor should an output from an actual run skip verification just because it reads nicely. What you want to take away is a workflow where you can judge right from wrong yourself, rather than an unexplainable stroke of good luck.
:::

:::detail[After completing the guide, what should be kept alongside it?]
Keep the link to the original page you used and the key checkpoints from your final review. That way, if your friend asks where a certain statement came from, you can locate the corresponding information; when you adapt the guide for a different reader later on, you'll also know which historical facts cannot be casually swapped out. There is no need to save every phrasing you tried, nor to turn every hesitation into a lengthy report. Keep what helps you continue the work next time: the deliverable, the source, and any items that still need confirmation.
:::

## Check yourself
Now adapt this short guide for someone who only wants to pick a single program to watch. Rewrite the request: keep the original source material, change the reader's purpose, and write down one condition that needs to be rechecked.

## In one sentence
**Connect the source material, deliverable, and check criteria, and you can move from “please write this for me” to “I know whether it was written correctly.”**

lessons.title: 三个回答都很肯定，你该相信哪一个？
lessons.content:
# 三个回答都很肯定，你该相信哪一个？

## 同一个问题，出现了不同答案

[OpenAI 的一篇研究介绍](https://openai.com/index/why-language-models-hallucinate/)记录过这样的情况：询问同一位研究者的博士论文题名，聊天工具给出了不同的肯定答案，而这些题名都不对。我们不需要再编三个假题名；真正的问题已经出现了——同一个事实被说成了几种不同版本。

## 先猜一下

如果你也遇到这种冲突，再让助手把答案说得更肯定，能补上哪一种缺少的信息？

先写下你的判断，再往下看答案。

## 答案

更肯定的语气不能补上论文的真实记录。你需要的是能够核对题名的材料，而不是另一种自信说法。

## 把“说得出来”与“查得到”分开

这类听起来像事实、实际没有对上事实的回答，常被叫作 AI 的“幻觉”。名字容易让人误会；你可以先把它理解成：它给出了具体说法，但没有相应依据支持。

先划出有冲突的那一项，再找能确认它的记录。暂时找不到，就把题名留作待核对，而不挑文风最好的一个。

:::detail[它说错了，是不是代表整份回答都不能用了？]
不一定。先把回答拆成你真正需要的几项，而不是一口气全信或全丢。论文题名不对，就不能把那个题名放进成品；文章的写作结构是否清楚，则可以另行判断。你也可以让助手把缺少依据的地方标出来，再围绕已核实的材料继续工作。这样，你没有因为一处错误而放弃所有帮助，也没有让一处写得顺的段落掩盖一个具体错误。关键是把错误定位到能检查的那一项。你现在知道它说出了多个版本，还不知道哪个事实成立，这正是应该补材料的位置，而不是要求它继续猜得更像真的。
:::

:::detail[为什么不能把几个答案投票，选最多的那个？]
重复出现的说法不一定来自新的证据。你连续问同一个工具，它可能仍然依靠同样的信息；即使换一种提问方式，也没有因此取得论文记录。投票能告诉你哪种说法出现得多，却不能替那种说法提供出处。你可以把不同答案当成提醒：这里值得查。但下一步应改变信息来源，比如找研究者本人或学校保存的论文资料，而不是只增加回答次数。这个方法也能用在其他任务上：同一张照片的日期出现冲突，就去看照片记录；同一场活动的时间不同，就去看对应活动的公告。所需的检查材料，取决于你正在判断的事实。
:::

把这些下一步动作分开：它们是在补充可核对材料，还是只改变回答的外观？

::play{#fluent-is-not-true-sort}

### 先处理那个没有依据的位置

你可以请求：“请指出题名来自哪份记录；若无法核对，就保留未知，不要补写。”这并不保证助手照做，但让你知道下一份结果要检查什么。

## 自检

**发生事实冲突时，补一份能核对的材料，比补一句更肯定的话更有用。**

en.title: Three Answers Are All Confident: Which One Should You Believe?
en.content:
# Three Answers Are All Confident: Which One Should You Believe?

## Different Answers to the Same Question

[An OpenAI research introduction](https://openai.com/index/why-language-models-hallucinate/) recorded such a situation: when asked for the title of the same researcher's doctoral dissertation, a chat tool gave different, confident answers—and none of these titles were correct. We do not need to invent three more fake titles; the real problem has already emerged—the same fact was stated in several different versions.

## Predict first
If you also run into this kind of conflict, what missing information could be filled in by asking the assistant to sound even more confident?

Write down your judgment first before reading on to the answer.

## Answer
A more confident tone cannot supply the dissertation's actual record. What you need is material that allows you to verify the title, not another confident statement.

## Separate What Can Be Said from What Can Be Verified

Responses like these that sound like facts but do not actually match the facts are often called AI "hallucinations." The name can easily be misleading; for now, you can understand it as: it provides a specific claim, but without corresponding evidence to support it.

First mark the item where the conflict lies, then look for records that can confirm it. If you cannot find them for now, leave the title as pending verification rather than picking the one with the best writing style.

:::detail[If it got something wrong, does that mean the entire answer cannot be used?]
Not necessarily. First break down the response into the specific items you actually need, rather than trusting or discarding everything all at once. If the dissertation title is wrong, you cannot put that title into your final work; whether the writing structure of the article is clear can be evaluated separately. You can also ask the assistant to mark where evidence is lacking, and then continue working around the materials you have verified. This way, you don't abandon all help because of a single mistake, nor do you let a smoothly written passage cover up a specific error. The key is to isolate the error to the item that can be checked. You now know it has stated multiple versions and you do not yet know which fact holds true; this is precisely where you should add material, rather than asking it to keep guessing in a way that seems more real.
:::

:::detail[Why can't we vote on the answers and pick the most common one?]
A recurring claim does not necessarily come from new evidence. If you ask the same tool repeatedly, it may still rely on the same information; even if you rephrase your question, it still hasn't acquired dissertation records. Voting can tell you which claim appears more frequently, but it cannot provide a source for that claim. You can treat different answers as a reminder: this is worth checking. But the next step should be changing the information source—such as looking for dissertation materials kept by the researcher or the university—rather than simply increasing the number of responses. This method can also be used in other tasks: when dates for the same photograph conflict, look at the photo records; when times for the same event differ, look at the announcement for that event. The verification material required depends on the fact you are judging.
:::

Separate these next steps: are they adding verifiable material, or merely changing the appearance of the response?

::play{#fluent-is-not-true-sort}

### Address the Unsupported Point First

You can ask: "Please point out which record this title comes from; if it cannot be verified, leave it as unknown and do not make anything up." This does not guarantee the assistant will comply, but it lets you know what to check in the next result.

## Check yourself
Two answers give different capture dates for the same photograph. What kind of material would you look for, rather than having it pick a date again?

## In one sentence
**When factual conflicts arise, adding verifiable material is more useful than adding a more confident statement.**

lessons.title: AI 说你做得好，它检查过哪一项？
lessons.content:
# AI 说你做得好，它检查过哪一项？

## 一句夸奖，和一次逐项检查

[OpenAI 曾公开回滚一个过于迎合用户的更新](https://openai.com/index/sycophancy-in-gpt-4o/)。这个实际事件提醒我们注意一种区别。

你正在改写 [NASA 的历史观月公告](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/celebrate-international-observe-the-moon-night-at-nasas-goddard-space-flight-center/)。下面两种评语是我们的编辑对照，不是那次事件中的模型原话：“写得非常好！”以及“日期还在，地点也在，但开始时间被删掉了。”

## 先猜一下

要判断这份改写是否保留了参加信息，你能从哪一种评语继续做出具体修改，为什么？

先写下你的判断，再往下看答案。

## 答案

第二种评语指出了检查过的项目和缺少的位置。第一种表达了赞同，却没有说明参加信息是否完整。

## 把喜欢与符合要求分开

你可以喜欢一段文字的语气，但它仍可能遗漏必要信息。先写下检查项，再要求助手逐项指出成品中的对应位置；缺了哪项，就写明缺了。

:::detail[是不是以后都不应该听AI的鼓励？]
鼓励可以帮助你继续写，问题在于不能把它当作另一种东西。你想知道这段话是否热情，语气评价有帮助；你想知道时间和地点是否保留，就要做内容核对。把两种需要分开，你不必拒绝所有赞美，也不会在被夸奖之后漏掉修改机会。比如一份通知读起来很自然，却少了时间，正确做法是保留已经写好的表达，再把必要信息补回去。如果每次听到“很好”就结束检查，错过的不是一个更严厉的老师，而是那一项实际没有被看过的条件。
:::

看两份编辑记录：一种只检查读起来是否自然，另一种检查参加信息。它们什么时候会作出相同判断？

::play{#agreement-is-not-a-check-contrast}

## 按你要的结果来提问

试写：“请按日期、地点、开始时间三项核对，把对应文字指出来；缺的项目直接写缺失。”检查结果出来后，你仍能自己对照原公告，而不只依赖它的评价。

:::detail[它逐项打了勾，就真的检查过了吗？]
打勾也可能只是另一种说法，所以最好同时要求给出对应位置。它说日期存在，你就在成品中找到日期；它说与原公告一致，你再对照原公告。这里的好处是检查变小了：你不再面对一句“整篇没问题”，而是面对三个能够分别确认的项目。若某项没有找到，就停在那一项修，而不是让它重新把整篇写得更漂亮。官方回滚事件只说明那次更新有迎合问题，不说明每个工具、每次鼓励都出错。你学到的检查方法，不靠猜助手是不是有意讨好你，而看它是否给出了可以继续核对的内容。

你还可以把检查写成一张小表：要求是什么，成品里哪句话满足它，原材料哪一处支持它。三列各做一件事；缺少对应位置就先留空，不把一个勾当成已经找到了文字。
:::

## 自检

你增加了“必须保留时区”这一项要求。昨天按日期、地点、时间完成的检查，还需要补哪一步？

## 一句话

**赞同说明它怎样评价你，逐项核对才说明成品是否符合要求。**

en.title: When the AI Says You Did Well, Which Item Did It Check?
en.content:
# When the AI Says You Did Well, Which Item Did It Check?

## A Compliment and an Item-by-Item Check

[OpenAI once publicly rolled back an update that was overly flattering to users](https://openai.com/index/sycophancy-in-gpt-4o/). This real-world incident reminds us to pay attention to a distinction.

You are rewriting [NASA's historical Moon observation announcement](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/celebrate-international-observe-the-moon-night-at-nasas-goddard-space-flight-center/). The following two comments are our editorial comparisons, not the model's actual words from that incident: "Exceptionally well written!" and "The date is still here, and so is the location, but the start time was removed."

## Predict first
To judge whether this rewrite preserved the attendance information, which comment allows you to proceed with concrete revisions, and why?

Write down your judgment first before reading on for the answer.

## Answer
The second comment pointed out which items were checked and what was missing where. The first expressed approval, but did not indicate whether the attendance information was complete.

## Separating Liking from Meeting Requirements

You can like the tone of a passage, yet it may still omit essential information. First write down your checklist items, then ask the assistant to point out the corresponding locations in the final draft item by item; if an item is missing, state clearly that it is missing.

:::detail[Should you stop listening to AI encouragement altogether?]
Encouragement can help you keep writing; the problem is that you cannot mistake it for something else. If you want to know whether a passage sounds warm, an evaluation of tone is helpful; if you want to know whether the time and location were preserved, you must verify the content. By separating these two needs, you do not have to reject every compliment, nor will you miss an opportunity to revise after being praised. For example, if an announcement reads naturally but is missing the time, the right move is to keep the wording you have already written and add the necessary information back in. If you stop checking every time you hear "Looks great," what you miss out on is not a stricter teacher, but the specific requirement that was never actually reviewed.
:::

Look at two editorial logs: one checks only whether the text reads naturally, while the other checks the attendance information. When will they make the same judgment?

::play{#agreement-is-not-a-check-contrast}

## Ask for the Outcome You Want

Try writing: "Please check against the three items—date, location, and start time—and point out the corresponding text; for any missing item, state directly that it is missing." Once the check results come back, you can still cross-check against the original announcement yourself rather than relying solely on its evaluation.

:::detail[If it checked off every item, did it really inspect them?]
A checkmark can also just be another form of phrasing, so it is best to ask for the corresponding locations at the same time. If it says the date is present, locate the date in the final draft yourself; if it says it matches the original announcement, cross-reference the original announcement yourself. The advantage here is that the check becomes smaller: instead of facing a blanket statement like "the entire piece has no issues," you face three items that can each be verified independently. If an item cannot be found, stop and fix that specific item, rather than asking it to rewrite the entire piece to sound prettier. The official rollback incident shows only that that particular update had a sycophancy issue; it does not prove that every tool or every bit of encouragement is flawed. The checking method you learned does not rely on guessing whether the assistant is intentionally flattering you, but on whether it provides content that you can continue to verify.

You can also format the check into a small table: what the requirement is, which sentence in the draft satisfies it, and which part of the source material supports it. Each of the three columns serves one function; if a corresponding location is missing, leave it blank for now, rather than treating a checkmark as proof that the text was found.
:::

## Check yourself
You added a new requirement: "The time zone must be preserved." What additional step is needed for the check completed yesterday covering date, location, and time?

## In one sentence
**Approval shows how it evaluates you, while an item-by-item check shows whether the draft meets the requirements.**

lessons.title: 画得像历史照片，就真是历史吗？
lessons.content:
# 画得像历史照片，就真是历史吗？

## 一幅很像真的画，还缺什么

[Google 在 2024 年暂停了 Gemini 的人物图像生成](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-image-generation-issue/)，并公开说明某些结果存在历史不准确等问题。另一方面，[NASA 的《地出》页面](https://www.nasa.gov/image-article/apollo-8-astronaut-bill-anders-captures-earthrise/)把一张实际照片与摄影者、日期和任务记录放在一起。

你要给历史展板挑图，也要给一个虚构故事挑插画。两处都希望图片清楚、好看。

:::figure[《地出》：NASA / 阿波罗8号 / Bill Anders，1968年12月24日。官方图像，非AI生成。]{#earthrise}

:::

## 先猜一下

除了画得像不像，你会用哪一项不同要求来决定这两个位置分别适合什么图片？

先写下你的判断，再往下看答案。

## 答案

历史展板需要可核对的记录身份；虚构故事可以使用清楚标注的想象画。两者的差别不在于哪张更漂亮。

## 先决定图片在证明什么

如果图片要告诉读者“这件事真的这样发生过”，就要查来源、日期和图像身份。NASA 的照片记录能帮助你核对《地出》，不能顺带证明任何一幅风格相似的新画。

创作一幅想象场景则是另一种任务，关键是不要把它的身份藏起来。

:::detail[图像有机构名字，就可以不再检查了吗？]
还不能。你需要找到这张具体图像所在的记录，而不是只看到某个机构的名字。标题、图片与说明要对应，原图与改编图也要分开。比如你裁剪了《地出》的一部分，仍能说明它来自哪张原图；如果另画了原图里没有的物体，就不能再把整个新画面叫作那张原始照片。来源的作用是帮助你知道正在看什么，而不是替所有相似图像盖章。Google 的历史事件提供了一个真实提醒，但不证明今天所有生成图片都有同一问题；判断眼前这张图，仍然要检查眼前这张图的身份。
:::

给这两个用途选择合适的图像来源与标注方式。

::play{#a-picture-is-not-a-record-weigh}

## 什么时候该反过来

如果你的任务是为虚构故事表现一个想象中的世界，就没有必要把创意限制成一张历史照片。可以创作，但要让读者看得出这是插画或改编，而不是现场记录。

:::detail[真实照片也可能让人产生错误印象吗？]
可能。即使照片本身真实，把它放到错误的年份、地点或事件旁边，也会产生错误理解。你因此要同时检查图和图注，而不是只检查文件有没有被生成。比如《地出》拍摄于绕月任务，把图注写成月面着陆现场，就改变了这张照片的历史身份。相反，一幅明确写着想象插画的作品，不是在声称它记录了某次真实事件。你要分开的，是创作与记录两种用途，以及文字有没有让读者把它们混淆；这比简单地把图片分成“漂亮的可信，不漂亮的不可信”更能保护你的成品。

你给图片加标题时，可以先写它的身份，再写它想表达什么。原始照片、裁剪图、根据照片另画的插画，需要不同说明。不要因为它们都与同一主题有关，就在成品里只保留一个没有区分的来源标签。
:::

## 自检

你把一张真实照片改画成带有想象物体的画面。标题和图注需要怎样说明它的身份？

## 一句话

**图片可以帮助想象，也可以记录事实，但两种身份必须让读者分得开。**

en.title: If It Looks Like a Historical Photo, Is It Really History?
en.content:
# If It Looks Like a Historical Photo, Is It Really History?

## What Is Still Missing from an Image That Looks Real

[Google paused Gemini's image generation of people in 2024](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-image-generation-issue/), publicly explaining that some results had issues such as historical inaccuracies. On the other hand, [NASA's Earthrise page](https://www.nasa.gov/image-article/apollo-8-astronaut-bill-anders-captures-earthrise/) places an actual photograph alongside its photographer, date, and mission records.

You need to choose an image for a history display board, and you also need to select an illustration for a fictional story. In both cases, you want the pictures to be clear and appealing.

:::figure[Earthrise: NASA / Apollo 8 / Bill Anders, 24 December 1968. An official image, not AI-generated.]{#earthrise}

:::

## Predict first
Aside from how realistic it looks, what different requirement would you use to decide what kind of picture is suitable for each of these two placements?

Write down your judgment first before looking down at the answer.

## Answer
A history display board requires a verifiable record identity; a fictional story can use a clearly labeled imaginative drawing. The difference between the two is not about which one looks better.

## First Decide What the Image Is Proving

If an image is meant to tell readers that 'this really happened this way,' you must check its source, date, and image identity. NASA's photographic records help you verify Earthrise, but they cannot by extension prove any new picture in a similar style.

Creating an imagined scene is a different kind of task; the key is not to conceal its identity.

:::detail[If an image has an organization's name, can you stop checking?]
Not yet. You need to find the record containing this specific image, rather than merely seeing an organization's name. The title, image, and caption must correspond, and original images must be kept distinct from adapted ones. For example, if you crop a portion of Earthrise, you can still explain which original image it came from; if you draw objects not present in the original photo, you can no longer call the entire new image that original photograph. The purpose of a source is to help you know what you are looking at, not to rubber-stamp every similar image. The historical event with Google offers a real reminder, but it does not prove that all generated images today share the same issue; evaluating the picture in front of you still requires checking that specific picture's identity.
:::

Choose suitable image sources and labeling methods for these two uses.

::play{#a-picture-is-not-a-record-weigh}

## When to choose the other way

If your task is to depict an imagined world for a fictional story, there is no need to restrict your creativity to a historical photograph. You can create freely, but make sure readers can tell it is an illustration or an adaptation, rather than an on-the-scene record.

:::detail[Can an actual photo also create a false impression?]
It can. Even if the photograph itself is genuine, placing it next to the wrong year, location, or event will create a misunderstanding. You therefore need to inspect both the picture and the caption, rather than merely checking whether the file was generated. For example, Earthrise was taken during a lunar orbit mission; writing the caption as a lunar landing site changes the photograph's historical identity. Conversely, a work clearly labeled as an imaginative illustration is not claiming to record a real event. What you need to separate are the two purposes—creation and documentation—and whether the text leads readers to confuse them; this protects your finished work much better than simply dividing pictures into 'the attractive ones are credible, and the unattractive ones are not.'

When titling an image, you can state its identity first, and then describe what it aims to express. Original photographs, cropped images, and illustrations redrawn from photos require different explanations. Do not keep only a single, undifferentiated source tag in your final product just because they are all related to the same topic.
:::

## Check yourself
You redraw an actual photograph into a scene that includes imaginary objects. How should the title and caption explain its identity?

## In one sentence
**Images can support imagination and record facts, but readers must be able to tell the two identities apart.**

lessons.title: 同一个聊天框，为什么不总是在做同一件事？
lessons.content:
# 同一个聊天框，为什么不总是在做同一件事？

## 一个输入框，后面可能是不同动作

你在聊天框里提出请求，最后都看见一个回答。[搜索功能的介绍](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-search/)谈网页来源，[Whisper 的介绍](https://openai.com/index/whisper/)谈语音转写，而 [Google 的图像问题说明](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-image-generation-issue/)还特意区分了聊天应用、搜索与底层模型。

“聊天框”是你接触它们的地方，却不直接告诉你背后完成了哪种动作。

## 先猜一下

如果你要查一份新发布的公告，仅仅知道工具能写出一段流畅文字，还缺少哪一种能力信息？

先写下你的判断，再往下看答案。

## 答案

你还需要知道它能否找到或读取那份公告。会组织语言，不等于已经取得所需的新材料。

## 用动作理解工具能力

先不用背一串名称。找网页，是检索；把已有声音写下来，是转写；按要求形成新文字或图像，是生成。一个产品可能组合这些动作，但一次回答是否真的使用了某项能力，还要看实际过程和材料。

:::detail[为什么不把这些统称为AI就好了？]
日常交流时统称 AI 没问题，但你要判断任务能不能完成时，就需要更具体一点。你要寻找今天的新公告，关键是能否取得那份公告；你已经有一份录音，关键是能否处理声音；你想把公开资料改成一张简洁卡片，关键是能否按要求组织文字。它们最后都可能出现在聊天框里，检查方式却不同。把动作点名，你就能问到真正缺少的能力，而不必猜某个产品是不是“足够聪明”。你也不用了解它内部有多少程序；只需知道它拿了什么材料、做了什么变化、交回了什么成品。
:::

读每张任务卡，把它放到最直接完成这个动作的工具类别里。三个类别对应真实产品说明中的检索、转写与生成。

::play{#which-tool-did-it-use-sort}

## 它不是什么

工具名称不是这一次工作的证明。页面有搜索功能，不等于你正在读的每一句都已经搜索过；产品能处理音频，不等于任意回答都来自一段真实录音。

:::detail[我怎样看出这次到底做了什么？]
先找可以观察的线索。请求使用你上传的文件，就看看结果是否对应那份文件；要求找网页，就打开它给出的来源；要求转写，就用原录音核对相应位置。某些工具会显示使用过的动作，这可以帮助定位，但不能代替结果检查。若页面没有足够线索，就把范围问清楚，比如“这项日期是从我提供的公告提取的，还是你没拿到原文？”不要因为回答里出现“已经核实”几个字就停止。你要找的是任务与材料的对应关系，而不是一个听起来专业的标签。对于当前功能是否可用，也应查看当前说明，不把历史发布介绍当成永久保证。

你也可以先把任务拆成两句：先找到那份公告，再按公告写介绍。拆开以后，若第一步没有取得材料，第二步就不能偷偷把缺少的事实编进一段漂亮文字。
:::

## 自检

一个工具可以生成图片，但你现在需要当天发布的交通公告。你首先应确认哪一项与这次任务有关的能力？

## 一句话

**不要只问它是不是AI，要问它拿到什么材料、做了什么动作。**

en.title: Why Isn't the Same Chat Box Always Doing the Same Thing?
en.content:
# Why Isn't the Same Chat Box Always Doing the Same Thing?

## One Input Box May Involve Different Actions Behind It

You make a request in a chat box, and in the end, you always see an answer. [The introduction to search](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-search/) discusses web sources, [the introduction to Whisper](https://openai.com/index/whisper/) discusses speech transcription, and [Google's explanation of image generation issues](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-image-generation-issue/) even specifically distinguished chat apps, search, and the underlying model.

"The chat box" is where you interact with them, but it doesn't directly tell you which action was completed behind the scenes.

## Predict first
If you want to check a newly released announcement, and only know that a tool can write fluent text, what kind of capability information is still missing?

Write down your judgment first before reading the answer below.

## Answer
You also need to know whether it can find or read that announcement. Being able to organize language does not mean it has already retrieved the necessary new material.

## Understanding Tool Capabilities Through Actions

You don't need to memorize a long list of terms first. Finding web pages is retrieval; writing down existing audio is transcription; creating new text or images according to requirements is generation. A product may combine these actions, but whether an individual response actually used a given capability still depends on the actual process and materials.

:::detail[Why not just call all of this AI?]
Referring to it broadly as AI is fine in casual conversation, but when you need to judge whether a task can be completed, you need to be more specific. If you are looking for today's new announcement, the key is whether it can retrieve that announcement; if you already have an audio recording, the key is whether it can process audio; if you want to turn public material into a concise card, the key is whether it can organize text as requested. They may all end up appearing in a chat box, yet the ways to check them are different. By naming the action, you can ask about the capability that is truly missing, rather than having to guess whether a product is "smart enough." You also do not need to understand how many programs run inside it; you only need to know what materials it took in, what changes it made, and what finished product it returned.
:::

Read each task card and place it into the tool category that most directly performs this action. The three categories correspond to retrieval, transcription, and generation in real product descriptions.

::play{#which-tool-did-it-use-sort}

## What it is not

A tool's name is not proof of its work this time. Just because a page has a search feature does not mean every sentence you are reading was searched; just because a product can process audio does not mean an arbitrary answer comes from a real recording.

:::detail[How can I tell what was actually done this time?]
First, look for observable clues. If a request uses a file you uploaded, check whether the result corresponds to that file; if you asked it to find web pages, open the sources it provides; if you asked for transcription, check the corresponding locations against the original recording. Some tools display the actions that were used, which can help with locating them, but cannot replace verifying results. If the page does not have enough clues, clarify the scope, such as: "Was this date extracted from the announcement I provided, or did you not get the original text?" Do not stop just because the words "already verified" appear in the answer. What you are looking for is the correspondence between the task and the materials, not a professional-sounding label. As for whether a current feature is available, you should also check current documentation, rather than treating historical launch announcements as permanent guarantees.

You can also break the task into two sentences first: first find that announcement, then write an introduction based on the announcement. Once split, if the first step did not obtain the material, the second step cannot sneak the missing facts into beautifully written text.
:::

## Check yourself
A tool can generate images, but right now you need a traffic announcement released today. Which capability relevant to this task should you confirm first?

## In one sentence
**Do not just ask whether it is AI; ask what materials it received and what actions it took.**

provenance.supports: Whisper作为一款语音识别系统推出，能够转录语音，并将其他语言的语音翻译为英语。
provenance.limitations: 语音识别并不能保证转录文本完全正确，也不能保证体现说话者的真实意图或事实真相。切勿虚构原始材料中未体现的录音、转录文本或错误。

en.supports: Whisper was introduced as a speech-recognition system that can transcribe speech and translate speech from other languages into English.
en.limitations: Speech recognition is not a guarantee of a correct transcript, speaker intent or factual truth. Do not invent a recording, transcript or error that the source does not show.

evidence.sourceTitle: Gemini image generation got it wrong. We'll do better.

provenance.locator: 事件经过
provenance.supports: 在生成了不准确且具有冒犯性的结果后，谷歌暂停了Gemini生成人物图像的功能。其官方解释将该对话式应用与谷歌搜索以及底层模型区分开来。
provenance.limitations: 这是一起历史产品事件，并不证明当前所有图像工具都会以同样的方式出错。并未重新发布该事件中生成的任何图像。

en.supports: Google paused Gemini's generation of images of people after inaccurate and offensive results. Its explanation distinguished the conversational app from Search and the underlying models.
en.limitations: A historical product incident, not evidence that all present image tools fail in the same way. No generated image from that incident is republished.

lessons.title: 表格排得整齐，合计就不会错吗？
lessons.content:
# 表格排得整齐，合计就不会错吗？

## 几个大数字，数的却不是同一种东西

[史密森尼管理的开放数据集条目](https://registry.opendata.aws/smithsonian-open-access/)记录2020年开放发布超过280万件二维、三维图像，并在机构背景中另列210万册图书与15.6万立方英尺档案。

你想把它们整理成一个小表，有人却把这些行统一命名成“使用人数”。先不做计算，看看列名发生了什么变化。

## 先猜一下

这些数字都来自同一机构，为什么仍不能直接填进同一个“人数”列？

先写下你的判断，再往下看答案。

## 答案

因为它们数的是不同对象，单位也不同；没有一项是在记录独立的人。统一列名没有把图像、图书或档案体积变成人数。

## 先读列名，再看数字大小

给每行保留三个问题：数的是什么、单位是什么、对应哪个时点。发布图像有明确事件日，机构背景中的其他数没有逐项统计日期，不能顺手填成同一天。

[数据分析说明](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8437071)介绍了整理数据与检查分析的操作。表格整齐与数值含义正确，是两种不同检查。

:::detail[为什么数字抄对了，表格仍然可能错？]
你抄下210万，却把旁边的册改成人，这行字说的就是另一回事了。把15.6万立方英尺写成15.6万件也一样：体积与件数不是同一个计数单位。数字需要和对象、单位一起搬动，不能只复制中间的一串字符。这里不需要复杂数学就能检查：先用一句完整的话读出每一行，再问原文是否真的这么说。工具可以很快排表，但你仍要给表头一个与材料相符的含义。
:::

:::detail[图像与物品都可以叫“件”，为什么也不能直接合计？]
相同计量词并不证明两个集合互不重叠或一一对应。一件实物可以有不同角度的数字图像，数字资料也不一定等同于实物数量。当前条目没有给你完整对应表，就不要自行为它们创造一个合计对象。你仍能分别列出发布图像与馆藏背景，只是不能把看起来相似的单位当成合计依据。若真正需要回答数字化覆盖比例，应另查对象一致、范围明确的统计，而不是把手头两串数直接相除。
:::

:::detail[以后遇到浏览或下载次数，也要这样查吗？]
同样先看它数的是什么。一次浏览是动作记录，一个人可能产生多次动作；下载次数也不自动等于独立下载人数。这里不是在补报史密森尼的使用统计，而是把单位检查的方法带到另一类记录。你应先找有没有按人去重的定义，找不到就保留次数，不用猜成多少人。能指出缺少哪一项定义，就已经比把所有大数字排成一张“用户增长表”更接近真实问题。
:::

把真实条目直接支持的记录，与改换了对象或单位的说法分开。

::play{#numbers-need-a-check-sort}

## 自检

另一份记录只给浏览动作次数，没有说明如何去重。你还缺哪种信息，才能把它写成独立人数？

## 一句话

**数字先要回答数的是什么，再值得讨论算得对不对。**

en.title: If a table is neatly arranged, does that mean the total won't be wrong?
en.content:
# If a table is neatly arranged, does that mean the total won't be wrong?

## Several large numbers, but they do not count the same thing

An [open dataset entry managed by the Smithsonian](https://registry.opendata.aws/smithsonian-open-access/) records the open release of more than 2.8 million 2D and 3D images in 2020, and separately lists 2.1 million books and 156,000 cubic feet of archives in the institutional background.

You want to organize them into a small table, but someone labels all these rows uniformly as "Number of Users." Without doing any calculations yet, look at what changed with the column names.

## Predict first
These numbers all come from the same institution, so why can they still not be entered directly into the same "Number of people" column?

Write down your judgment first before looking at the answer below.

## Answer
Because they count different objects and use different units; not a single one records individual people. Unifying the column name does not turn images, books, or archive volume into people.

## Read the column names first, then look at the numbers

Keep three questions for each row: what is being counted, what is the unit, and what point in time does it correspond to? The released images have a clear event date, but the other numbers in the institutional background do not have item-by-item statistical dates, so you cannot casually fill them in as the same day.

The [data analysis guide](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8437071) introduces steps for organizing data and checking analysis. A neat table and correct numerical meaning are two different checks.

:::detail[Why can a table still be wrong even if the numbers are copied correctly?]
If you copy down 2.1 million but change the "volumes" next to it to "people," that row says something completely different. Writing 156,000 cubic feet as 156,000 items is the same: volume and item count are not the same unit of measurement. Numbers must be moved together with their object and unit, rather than just copying the string of digits in the middle. You do not need complex math to check this: first read each row as a complete sentence, then ask whether the original text actually says that. Tools can format tables quickly, but you still need to give the header a meaning that matches the material.
:::

:::detail[Images and physical objects can both be called "items," so why can't they be totaled directly either?]
Using the same unit word does not prove that two sets do not overlap or correspond one-to-one. A single physical object can have digital images from different angles, and digital materials do not necessarily equal the number of physical items. Since the current entry does not give you a complete correspondence table, do not invent a combined total on your own. You can still list the released images and collection background separately; you just cannot treat seemingly similar units as a basis for totaling them. If you truly need to answer the digital coverage ratio, you should consult separate statistics with consistent objects and a clear scope, rather than simply dividing the two numbers at hand.
:::

:::detail[When encountering view or download counts in the future, should they be checked this way too?]
Similarly, look first at what is being counted. A view is an action record, and one person may generate multiple actions; download counts also do not automatically equal the number of unique downloaders. This is not about supplementing Smithsonian usage statistics, but about bringing the unit-checking method to another category of records. You should first look for a definition that deduplicates by person; if none is found, keep the action counts rather than guessing how many people they represent. Being able to point out which definition is missing already brings you closer to the real issue than arranging all large numbers into a "user growth table."
:::

Separate records directly supported by the original entry from claims that altered the object or unit.

::play{#numbers-need-a-check-sort}

## Check yourself
Another record gives only the number of view actions without explaining how they were deduplicated. What kind of information are you still missing before you can write it as a count of unique individuals?

## In one sentence
**A number must first answer what it is counting before it is worth discussing whether the calculation is correct.**

provenance.locator: 资料说明、管理者、许可与引用说明
provenance.supports: 由SI管理的数据集说明记录了2020年2月25日发布超过280万件CC0二维、三维图像及相关元数据和研究数据的事件。它在机构背景中另列1.55亿件物品、210万册图书和15.6万立方英尺档案，并标明管理者为SI。这些数量的对象与单位不同，不是独立使用人数。
provenance.limitations: 条目未给页面自身的发布日期。2020年日期属于发布事件；机构背景中的馆藏数没有逐项独立统计日期。不能把不同单位相加、推算数字化比例，或把这些数量写成下载量与人数。CC0说明针对所述数据集，不是网络上全部内容。

en.locator: Description, Managed By, License and How to Cite
en.supports: The SI-managed dataset description records the February 25, 2020 release of over 2.8 million CC0 2-D and 3-D images with related metadata and research data. It separately describes 155 million objects, 2.1 million library volumes and 156,000 cubic feet of archives in its institutional context. It names SI as manager. These are different kinds of quantities, not unique users.
en.limitations: The entry has no publication date for the page itself. The release date belongs to the release event; collection-context counts do not all have a separately stated census date. Do not add unlike quantities, infer digitization percentages or label downloads/users with these counts. CC0 applies to the described dataset, not everything online.
