lessons.title: 换成一个新任务，你能独立走完整条路吗？
lessons.content:
# 换成一个新任务，你能独立走完整条路吗？

## 轮到你决定一个小成品

你已经见过[NASA保存的《地出》照片](https://www.nasa.gov/image-article/apollo-8-astronaut-bill-anders-captures-earthrise/)，也读过[2023年观月夜的公开公告](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/celebrate-international-observe-the-moon-night-at-nasas-goddard-space-flight-center/)。现在不再沿用前面的现成请求：从这两份真实材料中选一份，为一个明确读者做一张小资料卡。

可以解释照片的画面与背景，也可以整理过去活动的安排。你自己的表达，与原始资料的身份要能分清。

:::figure[《地出》：NASA / 阿波罗8号 / Bill Anders，1968年12月24日。官方图像，非AI生成。]{#earthrise}

:::

## 先猜一下

在真正写卡片之前，你会怎样安排材料、请求和检查，才能让另一个人接着完成？

先写下你的判断，再往下看答案。

## 答案

先选一个读者和成品，列出对应的原始材料，再写需要保留与检查的条件。把还没确认的内容留明，不用额外编写来让卡片显得完整。

## 完成自己的第一张任务单

写下三小段：“给谁、做什么”“使用哪份材料”“交付前核对什么”。然后按这张任务单写出两三句卡片说明，或交给你已有的AI工具帮助起草。

无论用了哪条路径，都回到原图或原文核对。没有实际调用工具，就把成果记为自己的编辑练习，不把它说成模型已经做过的任务。

:::detail[这次为什么不再给一份完整的请求让你照抄？]
你前面已经练过给成品命名、提供合适材料、检查具体信息。最后这一步要把它们放到同一个小任务里，让你自己决定先后与取舍。你仍可查看来源和前面的提示，但应能说出每一项要求为什么在这里。只抄一份完整请求，也许能得到不错的文字，却不容易看出你是否知道哪一项需要随任务更换。把自己的版本保留下来，再用另一个材料重做一次，比把同一段话润色很多遍更能暴露还没弄清的地方。
:::

最后一次选择帮助程度：看你实际做到哪一步，决定继续独立做，还是回到一个更小的示范。

::play{#your-first-ai-method-weigh}

## 什么时候该反过来

如果连选定材料的一段话都还读不懂，就先缩小到那一段，回看一个示范或请求适量帮助。独立完成不是禁止求助，而是知道自己缺哪一步。

:::detail[怎样知道作品可以交出了，而不是永远修改？]
回到你开始时写的检查条件。图卡要让读者看懂画面与背景，就分别检查可见内容、作者日期和原始链接；活动卡要说明过去的安排，就核对年份、地点与参加方式。当这些条件已满足，停止增加无关背景。若后来新增一项事实，再为那一项补查，而不是假定旧检查覆盖了所有新内容。你获得的是一份范围明确的作品，不是对主题无所不包的永久结论。
:::

:::detail[准备公开分享，还要多看哪一项？]
查看素材自身的使用说明，并把原始资料与自己的编辑区分开。[NASA的媒体使用指导](https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/)说明了署名、第三方内容及机构标识等边界，不能由一张能下载的照片推断所有素材都任意可用。使用这张照片时保留适当出处，不暗示NASA审阅或认可了你的卡片。若换成另一张现代照片，重新查看那张图的权利信息；你已经学会的检查方法可以复用，素材许可本身不能从旧任务直接搬过去。
:::

## 自检

把这张卡换成另一份真实公开材料，不照抄原来的年月日与说明。你能否重新指出读者、成品、来源和一个需要检查的地方？

## 一句话

**能换材料重新完成同一种判断，才说明方法开始属于你自己。**

en.title: If You Switch to a New Task, Can You Walk the Entire Path on Your Own?
en.content:
# If You Switch to a New Task, Can You Walk the Entire Path on Your Own?

## Your Turn to Decide on a Small Deliverable

You have already seen [the "Earthrise" photo preserved by NASA](https://www.nasa.gov/image-article/apollo-8-astronaut-bill-anders-captures-earthrise/) and read [the public announcement for the 2023 Observe the Moon Night](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/celebrate-international-observe-the-moon-night-at-nasas-goddard-space-flight-center/). Now, instead of reusing the ready-made requests from before: choose one of these two real-world materials to create a small information card for a specific reader.

You can explain the image's visuals and background, or organize the arrangements of the past event. You must clearly distinguish your own expression from the identity of the original source material.

:::figure[Earthrise: NASA / Apollo 8 / Bill Anders, 24 December 1968. An official image, not AI-generated.]{#earthrise}

:::

## Predict first
Before you actually write the card, how would you arrange the materials, request, and checks so that another person could pick it up and complete it?

Write down your judgment first, then scroll down to see the answer.

## Answer
First select a reader and a deliverable, list the corresponding source materials, and then write down the conditions that must be preserved and checked. Leave unconfirmed details clearly noted rather than making things up just to make the card look complete.

## Complete Your First Task Sheet

Write down three short sections: "For whom and what to make," "Which material to use," and "What to verify before delivery." Then, follow this task sheet to write two or three sentences of card copy, or hand it to an AI tool you already use to help draft it.

Whichever path you take, return to the original image or original text to verify. If you did not actually call a tool, record the result as your own editing exercise rather than describing it as a task the model has already performed.

:::detail[Why are we no longer giving you a complete request to copy this time?]
Earlier, you practiced naming deliverables, providing appropriate materials, and verifying specific information. This final step brings them together into a single small task, letting you decide the sequence and trade-offs yourself. You can still consult the sources and earlier hints, but you should be able to explain why each requirement is there. Simply copying a complete request might yield decent text, but it will not easily show whether you know which items need to change with the task. Keeping your own version and redoing it once with different material will expose what you have not yet figured out far better than polishing the same paragraph many times.
:::

Choose your level of assistance one last time: based on how far you actually got, decide whether to continue independently or return to a smaller demonstration.

::play{#your-first-ai-method-weigh}

## When to choose the other way

If you cannot yet understand even a single paragraph of the selected material, narrow your focus to that paragraph first, review a demonstration, or request a moderate amount of help. Working independently does not forbid asking for help; it means knowing which step you are missing.

:::detail[How do you know work is ready to hand off rather than being revised forever?]
Return to the verification conditions you wrote at the start. If an image card is meant to help readers understand the visuals and background, check the visible content, creator and date, and original link; if an event card is meant to explain past arrangements, verify the year, location, and participation details. Once these conditions are met, stop adding irrelevant background. If you add a new fact later, look up that specific item instead of assuming earlier checks cover all new content. What you obtain is a piece of work with a well-defined scope, not an all-encompassing, permanent conclusion on the topic.
:::

:::detail[What additional item should you check before sharing publicly?]
Check the material's own usage instructions, and distinguish the original source material from your own edits. [NASA's Media Usage Guidelines](https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/) explain boundaries such as attribution, third-party content, and agency identifiers; you cannot infer that all assets are freely usable simply because a photo can be downloaded. When using this photo, retain appropriate attribution and do not imply that NASA reviewed or endorsed your card. If you switch to another modern photograph, recheck the rights information for that image; the verification methods you have learned can be reused, but the asset license itself cannot simply be carried over from an old task.
:::

## Check yourself
Switch this card to another real public material without copying the original dates or descriptions. Can you once again identify the reader, deliverable, source, and one item that needs checking?

## In one sentence
**Only when you can switch materials and repeat the same judgment does the method truly start to become your own.**
